legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Quoted directly from Customs: "You may bring into Serbia as much money as you wish, but if it is EUR 10.000 or more (in dinars or other foreign currency) your obligation is to DECLARE it to Customs, the same as you would do when entering/leaving EU." On departure, all passengers may take out up to EUR 10,000 freely; Serbian residents may not exceed that without evidence of prior import/withdrawal, and non-residents may exceed it only with specific receipts (a customs cash-declaration form from entry, a Serbian bank withdrawal receipt, or an exchange-office receipt for RSD obtained via card use in Serbia).

notes: Applies per person, including children (Customs FAQ: "It applies to each person, children included"). Get and keep the Cash Declaration Form at entry if you're carrying a large sum you might need to take back out — without it, an amount over EUR 10,000 on departure risks seizure. Payment cards can be brought in/out freely with no limit.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Quoted directly from Customs: medicines may be brought in "for personal passenger's use and for animals accompanying the passenger, in quantity needed for regular therapy not longer than 15 days. In that case medical opinion won't be necessary." For a longer stay, "a larger quantity of medicines required for the implementation of usual therapy during several months of stay (more than 15 days, but no more than six months)" is allowed but needs prior approval from "the competent ministry" (the Ministry of Health).

notes: Above a 15-day supply, or if the medicine contains a controlled psychoactive substance, or if a single package exceeds 30 dosage units, Customs specifically flags that pre-approval is required — see the dedicated controlled-medication entry for Serbia for that stricter case.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Quoted directly from Customs: "if medicines that you use contain controlled psychoactive substances and/or if their quantity exceeds one package of up to 30 dosage units, you should obtain the approval for import of medicines for personal needs from the competent ministry" — i.e. the general 15-day/no-approval rule does not apply once a controlled substance is involved; approval from the Ministry of Health is needed regardless of how short the trip is.

notes: Customs' own FAQ doesn't name which specific drugs count as "controlled psychoactive substances" — that's set by Serbia's Law on Psychoactive Controlled Substances (Zakon o psihoaktivnim kontrolisanim supstancama) schedules, which weren't read directly in this pass. Treat common stimulants (Adderall/Vyvanse/Ritalin) and benzodiazepines (Xanax/Valium) as likely to trigger this approval requirement, and apply for approval before travel rather than assuming a 15-day rule applies.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Cannabis is classified as a Schedule I narcotic drug under Serbia's Law on Psychoactive Controlled Substances (Zakon o psihoaktivnim kontrolisanim supstancama); unauthorized production, sale and possession are criminalized under Criminal Code Arts. 246 and 246a, including for small personal-use quantities. There is no legal personal-import pathway or medical-use exception for travelers.

notes: This row is sourced to a law firm's country guide (CMS Expert Guides), not Serbia's own statute text directly — the Criminal Code articles and the Psychoactive Controlled Substances Law schedules weren't read verbatim in this pass. Reported penalty range for unauthorized possession of larger/dealing quantities is 3-12 years' imprisonment (Art. 246); simple possession of a small personal-use quantity (Art. 246a(1)) can draw a fine or up to 3 years, with a possibility of exemption from punishment in some cases. Do not bring cannabis into Serbia in any form.

legal_source.name: CMS Expert Guides — Cannabis Law and Legislation in Serbia

limits.description: Legal hemp cultivation exists in Serbia (fibre, seed and further-propagation use, THC capped at 0.3%, requiring Ministry of Agriculture authorisation), but according to CMS Expert Guides, "the extraction of CBD oil is not regulated by law" and Serbia's Commission for Psychoactive Controlled Substances has given an opinion that CBD itself is a psychoactive substance capable of unwanted effects.

notes: This is genuinely ambiguous, not a confirmed personal-import rule — sourced to a law firm's country guide (CMS Expert Guides) and a hemp-industry site (Hemppedia), not Serbia's own regulatory text read directly. Given the Commission's stated position, don't assume a CBD product is safe to bring into Serbia just because it's legal where you bought it; treat it with the same caution as cannabis until you've confirmed current status with Serbian authorities.

legal_source.name: CMS Expert Guides — Cannabis Law and Legislation in Serbia

limits.description: Quoted directly from Customs: food "may only be brought into/taken out of country in reasonable quantities for personal use and in the original manufacturer's wrapping. If you are importing food of animal origin, its quantity is limited to a maximum of one kilogram."

notes: The 1 kg cap applies specifically to food of animal origin (meat, dairy, etc.); it must also be in its original, manufacturer-sealed packaging, not home-made or repackaged.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Customs' general food rule: goods "may only be brought into/taken out of country in reasonable quantities for personal use and in the original manufacturer's wrapping." Unlike animal-origin food, no numeric cap is stated for plant products in this source, and no phytosanitary-certificate requirement for fresh fruit, vegetables, seeds or live plants is mentioned.

notes: This is the general food rule, not a plant-specific one — Customs' tourist FAQ doesn't separately address live plants, seeds for planting, or phytosanitary certificates, so treat this as an open question rather than a confirmed answer for anything beyond ordinary packaged food. Check with Serbian phytosanitary authorities (Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management) before bringing live plants or seeds.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Quoted directly from Customs: "Passengers are not allowed to carry weapons across the border unless they possess the permit issued by a competent authority" (the Ministry of Domestic and Foreign Trade). An exception exists for hunting weapons and ammunition, which may be brought in temporarily "in appropriate quantities" specifically for organized hunting tours or shooting-sport events.

notes: Ordinary tourists have no general route to bring a firearm without a permit obtained in advance. The hunting/shooting-sport exception is narrow — it applies to participation in an organized event, not general recreational carrying. Blades/knives aren't separately addressed in this source.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Quoted directly from Customs: whether a permit is needed to import/export a drone "depends on whether it, in terms of its technical characteristics, meets the conditions prescribed in the National Control List of Dual Use Items and the National Control List of Weapons and Military Equipment." The permit, if needed, is issued by the Ministry of Internal and Foreign Trade. A list of UAV models exempt from the permit requirement exists in the Ministry's own "Instructions for the identification of UAV" document, which wasn't read in this pass.

notes: This is a customs/export-control classification, not a flight-registration rule — it governs whether your specific drone model can cross the border with or without a permit, based on its technical specifications, not where or how you fly it once in Serbia. If your drone isn't clearly on the exempt list, Customs says to contact the Ministry directly for a classification opinion before travel.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration of the Republic of Serbia — Passenger Customs Clearance FAQ (Tourists)

limits.description: Inward passengers aged 18 or over may bring in "alcoholic beverage 1.5 liters or less" duty-free. Above that, up to a total of 5 liters may be brought in with duty paid. Alcohol from Mainland China is treated more strictly: "limited to only 1 liter of controlled alcoholic beverage imported from Mainland China" even within the paid-duty allowance.

notes: Passengers exceeding the duty-free limit but within the 5-liter ceiling must use the Red Channel and pay duty rather than being refused entry outright; amounts above 5 liters in total are not addressed on this page.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Regulations for Inbound Passengers Carrying Tobacco or Liquor

limits.description: Passengers aged 20 or over may bring in duty-free: "200 cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 1 pound of tobacco, or 200 designated tobacco products" (the last covering products like heated-tobacco sticks that aren't cigarettes/cigars/loose tobacco).

notes: Passengers under 20 are not entitled to this concession at all. Fines for bringing in undeclared amounts above the allowance: NT$500 per carton of cigarettes, NT$3,000 per pound of tobacco, and NT$4,000 per 25 cigars. Vaping devices and e-liquid are a completely separate, much stricter rule — see the e-cigarettes entry for Taiwan; they are not covered by this tobacco allowance at all.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Regulations for Inbound Passengers Carrying Tobacco or Liquor

limits.description: Taiwan sets hard caps, not just declaration thresholds, on two currencies: "Each passenger can't bring more than NT$100,000 with him/her when entering or leaving Taiwan" and separately "Renminbi is limited up to RMB$20,000" — amounts above either cap cannot be brought in at all, even with a declaration. Other foreign currencies work differently: amounts "in excess of US$10,000 (or its equivalent in other foreign currencies) must be declared," but there is no maximum once declared. Negotiable securities with a face value over US$10,000 must also be declared, with no cap.

notes: This is a genuinely unusual rule most travelers don't expect: New Taiwan Dollars and Renminbi are capped by law, while every other currency (USD, EUR, etc.) has no cap at all as long as it's declared above the USD 10,000-equivalent threshold. Failing to declare excess declarable currency results in confiscation of the excess portion.

legal_source.name: Kaohsiung Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Limits on NTD, RMB, Foreign Currency and Negotiable Securities Carried by Passengers

limits.description: Non-prescription (OTC) medicine: "maximum 12 units per type, 36 total units combined" (bottles/boxes/tubes as packaged). Prescription medicine without a doctor's note or prescription copy: "restricted to a 2-month supply." Prescription medicine with a doctor's note/prescription copy: up to a "maximum 6-month supply," not exceeding the documented reasonable dose.

notes: Must be in original packaging and for personal use only — reselling imported personal medication draws a fine of NT$30,000 to NT$2,000,000 under Pharmaceutical Affairs Act Arts. 27 and 92. Narcotic/psychotropic controlled medications follow a stricter, separate rule — see the controlled-medication entry for Taiwan.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Health and Welfare (Taiwan) — Rules for Bringing Everyday Travel Medication In and Out of the Country

limits.description: For personal Schedule 1-3 controlled drugs (examples the Ministry gives: sleeping pills like zolpidem, triazolam, flunitrazepam, and opioids like morphine and fentanyl), "the amount cannot exceed that on the prescription," a medical institution certificate or a diagnostic certificate/prescription copy from the attending physician is required, and the total is capped at a 6-month supply. For Schedule 1-3 controlled drugs specifically, travelers may send TFDA "a declaration and medical diagnostic certificate to apply for a certification document" in advance under Article 18 of the Enforcement Rules for the Controlled Drugs Act.

notes: The Ministry's own guidance does not name ADHD stimulants (methylphenidate/Ritalin, amphetamine-class drugs like Adderall or Vyvanse) specifically — whether they fall under this controlled-drug process or a different one wasn't confirmed in this pass, so don't assume either way; check with TFDA before travelling with any stimulant medication. Controlled drugs must be carried on the person at all times and cannot be sent by mail or courier.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Health and Welfare (Taiwan) — Pay Attention to Carrying Controlled Drugs Into and Out of a Country

notes: "Marijuana is still listed under the Category two narcotics in accordance with 'Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act' in Taiwan." "Offenders of manufacturing, transporting, selling, cultivating, transferring, possessing or taking Category two narcotics are subject to life imprisonment or a minimum ten-year fixed-term imprisonment, and may also be subject to a fine of no more than fifteen million New Taiwan dollars." There is no recreational or medical exception, and Taiwanese customs authorities have specifically warned travelers not to bring in cannabis products even from countries where cannabis is legal (e.g. Thailand).

legal_source.name: Taipei Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Taipei Customs Urges the Public Not to Import Cannabis and Its Related Products

limits.description: Taiwan applies an unusually strict THC threshold: if a CBD product's THC content exceeds 10 parts per million (0.001%) — far stricter than the 0.2-0.3% thresholds used in the US, EU, Japan or Thailand — it is classified as a Category 2 narcotic under Appendix 2 of the Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act and treated the same as cannabis itself. Even below that threshold, importing a CBD product without prior Taiwan FDA (TFDA) approval is illegal: "violating the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act results in imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to 100 million NT dollars" for unauthorized import of an unapproved drug.

notes: No CBD-containing product is currently approved for sale in Taiwan, so there is effectively no personal-use import pathway without a doctor's prescription and an advance TFDA application under the Regulations on Management of Medicament Samples and Gifts. Treat any CBD product as high-risk to bring into Taiwan, including hemp-derived products marketed as low-THC elsewhere.

legal_source.name: Taichung Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Importing CBD Products Without Permission Can Lead to Penalties

limits.description: "Almost all kinds of meat products made from land animals are NOT permitted to carry into Taiwan." The fine for bringing in undeclared meat products generally is "NTD 10,000 to NTD 1,000,000" under infectious-disease-prevention law. Pork specifically is under a further, harsher rule: Taiwan has "banned the import of all kinds of pork products from ASF [African Swine Fever]-infected areas," with a first-time violation fined at a flat "NTD 200,000, regardless of nationality," rising toward NT$1 million for repeat violations; foreign nationals who don't pay the fine at the border are repatriated.

notes: Taiwan detected its first-ever domestic African Swine Fever case in October 2025, so enforcement has tightened further. This page does not separately address dairy products — treat dairy as an open question rather than assuming it's exempt from the general animal-product restriction.

legal_source.name: Taipei Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — What Food Products Can I Bring Into Taiwan (African Swine Fever Prevention)

limits.description: "禁止攜帶活植物及其生鮮產品" ("Bringing live plants and fresh plant products is prohibited"), with an exception only for items that separately comply with plant quarantine regulations. Fresh fruit specifically has been banned from passenger baggage since 1 October 1998.

notes: Dried plant products (dried flowers, dried vegetables, dried fruit, dried spices) and some seeds (e.g. vegetable and spice seeds) can be brought in after declaring at the quarantine counter and passing inspection — this is a genuinely different, less strict rule than for fresh produce, so don't assume all plant matter is banned. The customs page mentions "severe penalties" for violations without stating an exact fine figure; a secondary source (Taiwan Ministry of Agriculture materials) cites NT$3,000 or more, but that specific figure wasn't independently confirmed on an official page in this pass.

legal_source.name: Taipei Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Agricultural, Livestock, Fishery Products and Food

limits.description: "Passengers are NOT allowed to carry e-cigarettes and e-liquids into Taiwan." Violators "may be fined between NT$50,000 and NT$5 million according to Paragraph 1 of Article 15 and Paragraph 2 of Article 26 of the Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act."

notes: Taiwan's amended Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act (in force since 22 March 2023) fully bans e-cigarettes — manufacture, import, sale and use — and separately regulates heated-tobacco products like IQOS, which are also barred for travelers to bring in. If merely transiting Taiwan for another destination, devices can be declared and deposited at the bonded luggage counter for collection on departure, rather than being confiscated outright.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Are Passengers Allowed to Bring Electronic Cigarettes into Taiwan?

limits.description: "Firearms (including shotguns, air guns, fishing guns, etc.), ammunition (including artillery shells, bullets, bombs, explosives, etc.), and knives referred to in the Act Governing the Control of Guns, Ammunition and Knives" are prohibited, "excluding those permitted by competent authorities."

notes: Taiwan has extremely strict, near-total gun control — private possession of firearms and ammunition is generally illegal outright, and there is no realistic tourist path to authorization. Secondary sources describe common traveler pitfalls beyond obvious firearms: switchblades, stun batons, gas-powered guns, cosplay prop knives, hunting knives, and toy guns with metal firing pins have all reportedly been confiscated; only plastic replica guns with no firing capability are generally treated as toys, though this specific distinction wasn't independently confirmed on the official customs page in this pass.

legal_source.name: Kaohsiung Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Prohibited Articles

limits.description: Drones with a maximum take-off weight over 250g must be registered with Taiwan's Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA) before flying (Regulations of Drone, Art. 6(1)); drones under 250g owned by an individual are exempt from registration. Foreign nationals bringing their own drone face an extra step regardless of weight class for anything requiring registration: under Art. 38(1)-(2), they must submit documents to the CAA and can only fly "after CAA's certification," and a foreign visitor holding valid drone credentials from their home country can get that certification valid for "a maximum of six month after the date of issuance."

notes: A tourist bringing a small recreational drone under 250g can fly without registering it at all, regardless of nationality. Operating a heavier drone (2-15kg with navigation systems, or anything over 15kg) also needs a Remote Pilot License with age/testing requirements on top of the registration/certification above — a materially higher bar than just registering the aircraft.

legal_source.name: Laws & Regulations Database of the Republic of China (Taiwan) — Regulations of Drone, Arts. 6, 38

limits.quantity: 1L spirits >22% ABV, or 2L ≤22% ABV/sparkling; plus 2L still wine and 10L beer

notes: Quoted directly from the General Directorate of Customs' own traveler page. Amounts above this are dutiable and must be declared.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Tobacco, alcoholic drinks and coffee

limits.description: Duty-free per traveler 17 or older: "200 cigarette" or "100 cigarillos" or "50 cigars" or "250 grams of smoking tobacco." "No relief for alcohol and tobacco shall be granted to travellers under 17 years old."
limits.quantity: 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos, or 50 cigars, or 250g smoking tobacco

notes: Quoted directly from the General Directorate of Customs' own traveler page. E-cigarettes are a separate matter — see the e-cigarettes entry for Albania, which has no equivalent explicit traveler allowance.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Tobacco, alcoholic drinks and coffee

limits.description: Travelers entering or leaving Albania "are obliged to declare the amounts in cash, any type of instrument negotiable of the holder, metals or precious stones, valuables and antiques, starting from the amount of 10,000 euros or its equivalent in other currencies."

notes: Quoted directly from the General Directorate of Customs' own traveler page. The threshold covers precious metals/stones and antiques as well as cash and negotiable instruments, and applies on both entry and exit.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Cash Declaration

limits.description: Foreign travelers may carry limited quantities of medicines for personal use if: (1) not for promotion/marketing, (2) they complete a written statement that the medication is for personal use and provide the prescribing doctor's contact details (Albanian or foreign), deposited with customs at the entry point, and (3) the amount covers no more than 2 months of treatment, justified by the accompanying doctor's prescription showing the daily dose. Non-residents' quantity should match the length of their stay in Albania.
limits.quantity: Up to a 2-month supply, with prescription and a customs declaration

notes: Quoted/paraphrased directly from the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' own page on this exact topic. This is the general-medicine rule; medicines classed as narcotic or psychotropic substances are far more restricted — see the controlled-medication entry for Albania.

legal_source.name: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (Republic of Albania) — Travel of foreign citizens with drugs for minimal consumption

limits.description: The Customs Authority's own prohibitions page states plainly: "It is prohibited the import, export, transit of narcotics and psychotropic substances" — a criminal offense under Albanian Criminal Law — and this explicitly extends to "plants, narcotic medicaments and psychotropic substances of natural or synthetic nature, their materials and their preparations."

notes: Unlike ordinary medication, the Customs Authority's page describing narcotics/psychotropic substances states a blanket import prohibition with no traveler or personal-medical-use exception mentioned. Some secondary/travel-advisory sources describe a narrower personal-use allowance for controlled medicines with a medical certificate, but that specific carve-out was not found on an Albanian government page in this research pass — do not assume it applies. If you take a medication that is a controlled substance in your home country, verify directly with the Albanian Embassy before travelling.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

limits.description: Covered by the same blanket ban as other narcotics: "It is prohibited the import, export, transit of narcotics and psychotropic substances," which explicitly extends to "plants, narcotic medicaments and psychotropic substances of natural or synthetic nature." A criminal offense under Albanian Criminal Law.

notes: Albania has had major real-world cannabis cultivation and trafficking enforcement over the past decade, and the Customs Authority's page names no medical or personal-use exception for travelers. There is no THC threshold or de minimis carve-out stated.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

limits.description: Not named specifically, but falls under the Customs Authority's blanket ban on importing "plants, narcotic medicaments and psychotropic substances of natural or synthetic nature, their materials and their preparations" — the same provision covering cannabis generally.

notes: No Albanian government page found that names CBD specifically or draws a distinction by THC content, unlike some countries' customs authorities. Given the blanket wording covering cannabis-plant preparations generally and no confirmed exception, treat CBD products the same as cannabis: do not bring them. This inference (CBD swept in under the general cannabis/narcotic-plant provision, not a CBD-specific rule) should be treated as somewhat less certain than the cannabis row itself.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

limits.description: "Foreign citizens have the right to enter with firearms in the territory of the Republic of Albania only after they are equipped with a temporary authorization issued by the competent body of the State Police." Category B and C weapons separately require State Police authorization for trading, import/export, hunting, or sporting purposes.

notes: You cannot simply bring a firearm into Albania — a prior temporary authorization from the State Police is required. The Customs Authority's page doesn't address bladed weapons, air weapons, or self-defense items specifically, so don't assume those are unregulated; the U.S. ITA country guide separately confirms "special import provisions are enforced for strategic sectors such as weapons, munitions."

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Weapons

limits.description: Albania's tobacco-control law (Law No. 9636, as amended through 2024) defines "smoking" to include electronic cigarettes, and permits their retail sale (18+ only) subject to restrictions — but the law's provisions found in this pass are about domestic manufacture, marketing and retail-sale channels (e.g., a ban on selling tobacco products, including via the definition covering e-cigarettes, "through the postal service"), not a traveler-facing import quantity.

notes: The Customs Authority's own traveler duty-free page (used for the tobacco and alcohol allowances above) does not mention e-cigarettes, vapes, or e-liquid at all — unlike tobacco, there is no stated personal duty-free allowance or explicit ban for travelers bringing a vape. Domestically, nicotine liquid may only be placed on the market in refill containers up to 10ml or disposables up to 2ml, with nicotine concentration capped at 20mg/ml — whether this domestic market-placement rule is enforced against a traveler's personal device wasn't confirmed. Treat this as unresolved rather than clearly allowed or banned.

legal_source.name: Law No. 9636, dated 6.11.2006 "On the Protection of Health from Tobacco Products" (as amended through 2024)

Travellers under 17 get no alcohol allowance. Anything over the allowance must be declared in the red channel.
limits.quantity: 1 L spirits or 2 L ≤22%; 4 L still wine; 16 L beer

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Travellers: dual channel system and general allowances

limits.description: Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos (max. 3 g each), or 50 cigars, or 250 g of smoking tobacco. Travellers under 17 get no tobacco allowance. Declare anything over the allowance in the red channel.

notes: Cyprus applies the EU's higher tobacco limit (Your Europe lists the countries applying the lower limit; Cyprus is not among them).

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Travellers: dual channel system and general allowances

limits.description: Anyone entering or leaving Cyprus with €10,000 or more in cash (or the equivalent in other currencies or bearer instruments such as traveller's cheques), or gold worth €10,000 or more, must declare it in writing to Customs at the point of entry or exit. Failing to declare is an offence: the cash or gold is seized and you can be fined up to €50,000.

notes: Cyprus Customs' page (last updated 2020) still cites the repealed Regulation (EC) 1889/2005; the current EU rule is Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 (EC DG TAXUD), which keeps the €10,000 threshold and defines cash as banknotes and coins, bearer negotiable instruments, gold coins of at least 90% gold and gold bars/nuggets of at least 99.5% gold. Cyprus' page also applies the declaration to travel to/from other EU member states (national Law 53(I)/2009).

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Cash Control; cross-checked with European Commission DG TAXUD — EU Cash Controls (Regulation (EU) 2018/1672)

limits.description: You cannot bring meat, milk or their products (including cheese) into Cyprus from outside the EU in your luggage. Fish, honey and powdered infant milk follow separate, more lenient EU limits.

notes: Conflict between sources, recorded per AGENTS.md §3.8: the EU rule (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122, directly applicable) allows fish up to 20 kg and honey up to 2 kg, but Cyprus Customs' restrictions list says meat, fish and cheese need authorisation from the Director of Veterinary Services and honey needs a Veterinary Services licence. The list may refer to commercial imports; if you plan to bring fish or honey, check with Cyprus Veterinary Services first. These rules don't apply to products coming from other EU countries, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino or Switzerland.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Personal imports of animal products (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122)

limits.description: Under EU rules you can bring, from outside the EU: fishery products up to 20 kg (or one fish, if heavier); other animal products such as honey up to 2 kg; and powdered infant milk, infant food or special foods needed for medical reasons up to 2 kg, if they don't need refrigeration before opening and are in unbroken branded packaging.

The list may refer to commercial imports; if you plan to bring fish or honey, check with Cyprus Veterinary Services first. These rules don't apply to products coming from other EU countries, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino or Switzerland.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Personal imports of animal products (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122)

limits.description: Plants, fruit, vegetables and cut flowers from outside the EU may not be brought in your luggage unless accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate. No certificate is needed for pineapples, coconuts, durians, bananas and dates. Cyprus Customs additionally requires a licence from the Director of the Department of Agriculture and a phytosanitary inspection for flowers and plants.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Trade in plants & plant products from non-EU countries (passengers' luggage; Regulation (EU) 2019/2072)

notes: Customs states its lists are not exhaustive and refers enquiries to the competent authority (Chief of Police).

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Prohibitions & restrictions (passengers)

limits.description: Visitors can bring small quantities of internationally controlled medicines (narcotics or psychotropics) for their own treatment only with a permit issued by Cyprus's Pharmaceutical Services (Ministry of Health). The application asks for your passport number, arrival and departure dates, and each drug's name, form, strength, daily dose and prescribed quantity, and must include a copy of your prescription showing the doctor's name, address, phone/fax and licence number. Without a permit, Customs treats narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and other controlled pharmaceuticals as prohibited imports.

notes: Apply to Pharmaceutical Services before you travel (phscentral@phs.moh.gov.cy). The Application Form for Import for Personal Use is linked from the source page.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Ministry of Health, Pharmaceutical Services — Narcotics and Psychotropics (permits for visitors carrying controlled medicines)

limits.description: Bringing a drone is not restricted, but flying it is regulated under EU (EASA) rules. Registration is needed if the drone weighs more than 250 g, or has a camera or other sensor able to capture personal data. Non-EU residents also need an A1/A3 remote pilot certificate (online training and exam, €15, valid 5 years) — not required for a C0 drone under 250 g. No flying in no-fly zones and keep at least 8 km from airports and heliports.

notes: If you already registered in another EU country (where you first flew), do not register again in Cyprus.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Department of Civil Aviation — Unmanned Aircraft (drones.gov.cy)

notes: Customs states its lists are not exhaustive; contact Customs Headquarters or the Police before travelling with any weapon.

legal_source.name: Passenger Services Directorate — Sri Lanka Customs

The NMRA page carries no visible date.

We could not find the content of NMRA's 'Schedule III' on an official page, so we cannot say which specific drugs (e.g. ADHD stimulants, benzodiazepines, codeine) are excluded. Art. 8: RPA/RPAS used in the Open or Specific category must be entered in the DGAC's Register of Remotely Piloted Aircraft (free, per NTC 001-2015) within 30 working days of acquisition. Art. 25/30: operations other than recreational use need an Open-category operating licence and a remote-pilot licence; the licence form asks for a DNI, passport or carné de extranjería. The regulation's Open/Specific-category provisions take effect only once the DGAC updates its technical rules (within two years), so NTC 001-2015 still governs in the meantime. notes: Same legal basis as alcohol: Decreto 1165 de 2019 Arts. 266 (10 units of the same class = not commercial), 268 (USD 2,000 franchise) and 270 (15% single tax on the excess). No separate litre/carton quota for this product appears in the customs decree: it simply counts toward the general duty-free allowance. What counts as one 'unit' (pack vs carton) is not defined in the decree — keep quantities clearly personal. Declare anything over the allowance on DIAN Form 530.

legal_source.name: Decreto 1165 de 2019 (Régimen de Aduanas), Arts. 266–270 – DIAN normograma

limits.description: Declare cash, Colombian pesos or monetary instruments over USD 10,000 (or equivalent) on DIAN Form 530, both entering and leaving.

notes: DIAN: travellers must file the 'Declaración de Equipaje, de Dinero o Títulos representativos de Dinero – Viajeros' (Form 530) when the amount in foreign currency, Colombian cash or monetary instruments exceeds 'USD 10.000 ... o su equivalente en otras monedas'; amounts up to USD 10,000 need no declaration. DIAN's Form 530 page states the same threshold. Cross-checked: gov.uk ('You can bring up to 10,000 US dollars-worth of any currency ... declare anything above this amount with ... DIAN'). Undeclared excess may be retained by customs (per DIAN Form 530 page; exact sanction not re-read).

legal_source.name: Trámites aduaneros – Viajeros – DIAN

limits.description: USD 2,000 of goods duty-free per adult (personal effects not counted); above that, up to USD 3,000 more with a 15% single tax if you were abroad at least 5 days (once a year).

notes: Decreto 1165 de 2019 Art. 268: duty-free accompanied baggage up to USD 2,000; personal effects are not counted. Art. 269: travellers abroad at least 5 calendar days may bring, paying the 15% single tax (Art. 270), up to 3 units each of household, sports and professional articles and up to 10 units of the same kind of other personal goods, up to USD 3,000 total, once per year per person. Art. 274: minors get a reduced quota (DIAN page: 50%). Art. 276: non-residents may temporarily import, tax-free and subject to re-export, items needed for personal or professional use during their stay if declared on arrival. DIAN's 'Trámites aduaneros' page repeats the USD 2,000 franchise and 15% tax. Note: the English version of DIAN's Form 530 page mentions a 'USD 5,000' quota that the Spanish page and the decree do not — the decree controls.

legal_source.name: Decreto 1165 de 2019 (Régimen de Aduanas), Arts. 266–270 – DIAN normograma

limits.description: No Colombian traveller allowance found. Carry personal quantities in original containers with a copy of your prescription; check legality yourself.

notes: No primary Colombian rule specific to travellers' personal medication was found (DIAN, INVIMA and the Fondo Nacional de Estupefacientes pages searched). Customs law treats 'efectos personales' — new or used articles a traveller may need for personal use during the trip — as outside the duty-free quota (Decreto 1165 de 2019, Art. 3 definition, as modified by Decreto 360 de 2021), but does not mention medicines. The UK government's Colombia travel advice says: 'If you take prescription medication, you will be responsible for determining its legality in Colombia. Always keep your medication in the original container, bring sufficient quantities ..., pack your medication in your carry-on luggage and carry a copy of your prescriptions', and that Colombian prescriptions 'must be written in Spanish, in the metric system and using the medicine's generic name'. travel.gc.ca adds that some prescription medicines are unavailable in Colombia and adrenaline auto-injectors are not sold there.

legal_source.name: Colombia travel advice – Health (updated 2026-10-06) – GOV.UK / FCDO

limits.description: Bringing cannabis into Colombia without a licence is a crime, even in transit and even in small amounts.

notes: Código Penal (Ley 599 de 2000) Art. 376 as modified by Ley 1453 de 2011: anyone who 'sin permiso de autoridad competente, introduzca al país, así sea en tránsito o saque de él' narcotic or psychotropic substances faces 128–360 months' prison; if the quantity does not exceed 1,000 g of marijuana or 200 g of hashish the penalty is 64–108 months. The only carve-out (added by Ley 1787 de 2016) is medical/scientific cannabis use under licences from the Ministry of Health or Ministry of Justice. Domestic 'personal dose' rules do not authorise import. CBD products are not specifically addressed by this source — treat as unverified. Travel advice (gov.uk) also stresses severe penalties for drug possession and trafficking.

legal_source.name: Ley 599 de 2000 (Código Penal), Art. 376 – Secretaría del Senado

limits.description: Sealed, commercially labelled cured/cooked meats, boneless aged hams and aged/processed cheeses up to 6 kg each; processed honey and pre-cooked shrimp up to 3 kg. Pork products from Spain and Germany currently banned.

notes: ICA (12 Apr 2017 notice, under Resolución ICA 3865 de 2005): animal-origin food may enter without an import document only in its original sealed packaging labelled with country, establishment, packing and expiry dates: cooked or cured hermetically packed sausages/meat products up to 6 kg; boneless hams up to 6 kg each (Spanish serrano aged >190 days, ibérico >365 days, Italian >400 days, others >180 days); aged, processed or spreadable sealed cheeses up to 6 kg; processed/pasteurised honey up to 3 kg; pre-cooked sealed shrimp up to 3 kg. Excluded: bovine meat products from BSE countries; cured pork from Italy and from countries with African or classical swine fever. Current restriction: ICA Resolución 00031675 (4 Dec 2025) Art. 3 prohibits pork products from Spain carried as accompanied baggage 'independientemente de la cantidad' (unless meeting OMSA Code art. 15.1.2), and Resolución 00034883 (30 Dec 2025) does the same for Germany, both until lifted. Non-compliant goods are held for re-shipment within 5 days or seized and incinerated. Declare animal products on the DIAN baggage declaration. Caveat: the quantity list comes from a 2017 ICA notice; no newer consolidated traveller list was found.

legal_source.name: El ICA hace recomendaciones a viajeros internacionales sobre el ingreso al país de productos de origen vegetal y animal (12 Apr 2017) – Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario (ICA)

limits.description: Plants, seeds, propagation material and fresh fruit/vegetables need a phytosanitary certificate from the origin country; otherwise they may be seized.

notes: ICA (12 Apr 2017 notice): products must arrive with 'el correspondiente certificado zoosanitario o fitosanitario' from the country of origin; plants of all species, planting/propagation material and fresh fruits and vegetables that don't comply may be seized because they can carry pests. Non-compliant goods are held for re-shipment within 5 days or seized and incinerated. Travellers must declare plants and plant products on the baggage declaration (DIAN lists 'vegetales, animales y productos reglamentados' among cases requiring Form 530). Caveat: 2017 notice; no newer traveller page found.

legal_source.name: El ICA hace recomendaciones a viajeros internacionales sobre el ingreso al país de productos de origen vegetal y animal (12 Apr 2017) – Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario (ICA)

legal_source.name: ARCA (Aduana) — ¿Cuál es la franquicia de ingreso?

limits.description: Entering with cash or monetary instruments (foreign or Argentine currency) worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared to customs on form OM 2249A. For under-16s the limit is USD 5,000. Amounts above USD 10,000 can only leave Argentina by bank transfer.

notes: ARCA 'Ingreso y egreso de valores': amounts under USD 10,000 may be brought in freely; higher amounts need a special declaration (OM 2249A). ARCA 'Régimen de equipaje' says to declare when 'igual o superior al equivalente a USD 10.000'. Conversion uses the Banco de la Nación buying rate at close of the previous business day. Cross-check: gov.uk Argentina advice says declare cash/travellers cheques over USD 10,000; Spain MFA says the same applies on entry and exit.

limits.description: Carry a legalised medical prescription. Under the Mercosur rule applied in Argentina, it must show your name and address; the medicine, active ingredient, strength, form, quantity and dosage; and the date, name, address, signature and registration of the prescriber. It must be authorised by the health authority. Patients in transit present this document to health or police authorities at the airport or border.

notes: Source: argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil summary of Mercosur GMC Resolution 66/2000, which ANMAT applies. It covers travel between Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Venezuela, and no official page was found on how travellers from outside Mercosur are treated, so confirm with ANMAT before travelling. ARCA lists 'Estupefacientes' as prohibited in baggage. ANMAT's control lists include methadone, hydrocodone and hydromorphone (narcotics, Ley 17.818) and amphetamine, alprazolam, clonazepam, diazepam and lorazepam (psychotropics, Ley 19.303). Methylphenidate was not checked. Medicines not registered in Argentina may need an ANMAT exceptional-access (RAEM-NR) authorisation; that procedure is for imports and may not cover a traveller's own supply.

legal_source.name: Argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil — Mercosur: Traslado de medicamentos (Resolución GMC 66/2000)

limits.description: Do not bring cannabis. Customs prohibits narcotics ('Estupefacientes') in baggage, and ANMAT lists cannabis, its resin, and cannabis extracts and tinctures as Lista I narcotics under Ley 17.818.

notes: Sources: the ARCA 'Objetos permitidos y prohibiciones' page, plus the ANMAT controlled-substances list (argentina.gob.ar/sites/default/files/estupefacientes_2016.pdf, linked from the ANMAT 'Listados' page): 'CANNABIS (Marihuana), su resina (Haschisch) y los extractos y tinturas de Cannabis — LISTA I. LEY 17818/68'. No official page read deals with CBD-only products for travellers. Because 'extractos y tinturas' are listed, treat CBD oils as prohibited unless ANMAT confirms otherwise. Argentina's medical-cannabis programme is for registered patients in Argentina and does not give foreign travellers an allowance.

limits.description: Prohibited: meat of any species, cured/processed meats, sausages, hams, honey and other bee products, homemade food, and any food without a label. Exceptions: canned fish, pork or poultry. Boneless Spanish serrano/ibérico ham, sliced or in pieces, is allowed if it is factory vacuum-packed and labelled. Allowed items must be packaged, labelled and in personal quantities.

notes: SENASA page 'Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos' (Resolution 295/1999). The Spanish-ham exception comes from Res. 655/2017. limits.description: Allowed in personal quantities if packaged and labelled by the producer under official health control: pasteurised milk, condensed milk, milk powder, yogurt, butter, dulce de leche, and cheeses made from pasteurised milk. Other dairy products and derivatives are on the 'not permitted' list.

notes: SENASA 'Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos' (Res. 295/1999). The page lists 'productos y derivados lácteos' as not permitted, apart from the authorised items above. Treat raw-milk cheese and unlabelled dairy as prohibited. Declare SENASA-regulated goods on arrival.

limits.description: Prohibited: fresh fruit and vegetables; flowers and garden plants; fruit, ornamental and forestry plants; plant parts such as seeds, roots and buds. Allowed in personal quantities if packaged and labelled: processed fruit and vegetables (in syrup, pickled, canned), roasted or salted nuts, jams, candied fruit, juices, sugar and oil.

notes: SENASA 'Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos' (Res. 295/1999). Also prohibited: animal feed, veterinary products, insects and microorganisms. A separate SENASA barrier also restricts some fruit and meat entering Patagonia from the rest of Argentina.

notes: German Foreign Office (Stand 09.10.2026): 'Bis zu 1 l Alkohol ... dürfen zollfrei mitgeführt werden.' Cross-checked with Japan MOFA (updated 22 Apr 2026): bringing more than 1 litre of alcohol into Jordan incurs duty; if you enter overland with more than 1 litre and plan to take it out later by air, you pay a cash deposit (JOD only) at the border, refunded when customs checks the alcohol on departure. Jordan Customs' own site (customs.gov.jo) was IP-blocked from our environment, so the controlling customs text was not read. Public drinking is banned outside some hotels and restaurants (France Diplomatie).

legal_source.name: Auswärtiges Amt — Jordanien: Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise (Einreise und Zoll)

If you have not received a permit before you arrive, the authorities will hold your drone at the airport. You can collect it when you leave Jordan.' Canada: 'You must obtain authorization before importing or operating a drone'; violations can mean imprisonment, fines or confiscation. CONFLICT: France Diplomatie says drones 'sont interdits à l'arrivée en Jordanie et sont systématiquement confisqués', and Germany lists drones among prohibited imports. The CARC publishes a 'Drones Operations Approval Application Form' (https://carc.gov.jo/en/drones). Treat a drone as not importable unless you hold CARC approval before you travel.

legal_source.name: 外務省 海外安全ホームページ — ヨルダン 安全対策基礎データ（通関・外貨申告）

limits.description: 5 litres of wine, aguardiente or liquor per adult traveller, duty-free, as part of baggage

notes: Art. 365(j) of the customs regulation (Decreto 44051-H) counts as duty-free traveller baggage 'Quinientos gramos de tabaco elaborado, cinco litros de vino, aguardiente o licor, por cada viajero mayor de edad y hasta dos kilogramos de golosinas.' The text does not mention beer separately; it says 'wine, aguardiente or liquor'. Baggage must be for personal use, not commercial. Anything above the allowance counts as goods other than baggage (see the US$500-equivalent allowance row) and must be declared on the Declaración de Viajero (art. 368).

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: 500 g of manufactured tobacco per adult traveller, duty-free, as part of baggage

notes: Art. 365(j) Decreto 44051-H: 'Quinientos gramos de tabaco elaborado … por cada viajero mayor de edad'. The regulation states the allowance by weight, not by number of cigarettes. Amounts above it must be declared and taxes paid. E-cigarettes are not covered by this row (see unverified).

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Declare cash and/or títulos valores (securities/bearer instruments) of US$10,000 or more (or the equivalent in other currency) when entering or leaving

notes: Art. 35 Ley 8204 as quoted in Decreto 44096: 'Al ingresar en el país o salir de él, toda persona, nacional o extranjera, estará obligada a declarar el dinero efectivo o los títulos valores que porte, si la cantidad es igual o superior a los diez mil dólares … (US$10.000,00) o su equivalente en otra moneda.' The 'Declaración de dinero en efectivo y/o títulos valores' form (issued by the Instituto Costarricense sobre Drogas) is available at the migration posts; it must be completed and signed before finishing immigration and handed to Customs (arts. 4, 8, 11, 17). Failing to declare, or declaring a different amount, means 'la pérdida inmediata del dinero en efectivo y/o títulos valores a favor del Instituto Costarricense sobre Drogas' (art. 5) — it does not stop you entering or leaving. The threshold is 'igual o superior' — exactly US$10,000 must be declared. Cross-check: GOV.UK also says declare cash/travellers cheques of US$10,000 or more.

legal_source.name: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44096-MP-H-MAG-MOPT-MGP-MSP, Reglamento al artículo 35 de la Ley N° 8204 (cash and bearer-instrument declarations) — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Medicines for your own use, in quantities consistent with your circumstances and needs, enter duty-free as baggage; controlled (narcotic/psychotropic) medicines have extra rules

notes: Art. 365(c) Decreto 44051-H includes in traveller baggage 'Medicamentos, alimentos, instrumentos, aparatos médicos, higiénicos o de tocador y artículos desechables utilizados con estos, en cantidades acordes con las circunstancias y necesidades del viajero.' Baggage must not be commercial. If your medicine contains a narcotic or psychotropic substance, see controlled-medication-cr: more than one month's supply needs Ministry of Health authorisation. Cross-check: travel.gc.ca advises keeping medicines in the original container, in carry-on, with paper and electronic copies of prescriptions.

limits.description: Up to one month of treatment: no authorisation needed. More than one month: Ministry of Health authorisation, applied for at least one month before travel. Never allowed: 1961 Convention List IV narcotics and fentanyl in ampoules

notes: Art. 57 Decreto 45161-S (2025): 'El Ministerio de Salud autorizará a los viajeros el ingreso o salida de preparados farmacéuticos que contienen estupefacientes o psicotrópicos cuando la cantidad supere un mes de tratamiento' — apply at least one month before travel with: ID copy (for digital filing), copies of the prescription and epicrisis and/or medical report issued no more than 3 months earlier stating diagnosis and prescribed medicines, and a copy of the purchase invoice if bought abroad. 'Si las cantidades son menores a un mes de tratamiento, esta autorización no es requerida. Los viajeros internacionales no pueden llevar consigo los estupefacientes incluidos en la Lista IV de la Convención Única de 1961 de Estupefacientes, ni fentanilo en ampollas aun cuando se permita su uso en el país de origen.' Which substances are controlled: the Ministry of Health 'Lista de sustancias sometidas a fiscalización nacional' (SCIJ, dated 11 Sep 2026; https://sinalevi.go.cr/ResultadosNormativa/Informacion?param1=107827&param2=152346&param3=1) lists, among others, METILFENIDATO, ANFETAMINA, DEXANFETAMINA, ALPRAZOLAM, CLONAZEPAM, DIAZEPAM, LORAZEPAM, ZOLPIDEM, OXICODONA, CODEINA, MORFINA and FENTANILO. Brand names in the search terms are mapped to those ingredients for search only (Adderall = amphetamine salts; Ritalin = methylphenidate; Xanax = alprazolam; Valium = diazepam); the sources name ingredients, not brands. Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) and tramadol were not found as entries in the list text read, so they are deliberately not named here.

legal_source.name: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 45161-S, Reglamento para el control de drogas, estupefacientes y psicotrópicas (17 Jun 2025), art. 57 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Medicines plus the medical instruments and disposable items used with them (syringes, pen needles) enter duty-free as baggage in quantities matching your needs

notes: Art. 365(c) Decreto 44051-H covers 'Medicamentos … instrumentos, aparatos médicos … y artículos desechables utilizados con estos, en cantidades acordes con las circunstancias y necesidades del viajero' — this is a general rule; it does not name insulin or GLP-1 brands. Insulin, semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro) are not narcotics/psychotropics, so the one-month controlled-medicine authorisation (Decreto 45161-S art. 57) does not apply to them as such. Keep the prescription with you; airline rules on carrying needles and cooling packs are separate from customs.

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Tourists may bring hunting shotguns/rifles (up to four different hunting/target guns) and 500 rounds as baggage, but only subject to the Ley de Armas y Explosivos permit rules

notes: Art. 365(k) Decreto 44051-H: 'Escopeta o rifles de caza y quinientos tiros, incluso hasta cuatro armas diferentes para cacería o para tiro al blanco … siempre que se demuestre, en forma fehaciente, que el viajero es turista. El ingreso de armas y municiones estará sujeto a las regulaciones que sobre esta materia establece la Ley de Armas y Explosivos.' limits.description: Goods that are not baggage are tax-free up to 500 Central American pesos in total customs value, once every 6 months, if you were out of Costa Rica at least 72 hours

notes: Art. 115 Ley 7557: 'Las mercancías que la persona traiga consigo, que no constituyan equipaje, no estarán sujetas al pago de tributos hasta por un monto de quinientos pesos centroamericanos … Para estos efectos, la persona deberá permanecer un mínimo de setenta y dos horas fuera del país y no tendrá derecho a disfrutar, de nuevo, de este beneficio hasta que hayan transcurrido los seis meses siguientes a su arribo.' Auswärtiges Amt (Stand 09.10.2026): 'Die Einfuhr von Drogen, Alkohol, pornografischen Materials sowie religiöser Bücher und Materialien ist strengstens untersagt.' Cross-checked: Japan MOFA lists 酒類（みりん等の調味料を含む） — alcoholic drinks, including cooking seasonings such as mirin — among prohibited imports; Nederland Wereldwijd: 'Neem geen alcohol en varkensvlees(producten) mee naar Qatar'; France Diplomatie also lists alcohol as prohibited. Inside Qatar alcohol is sold only in licensed hotels/restaurants/bars and to resident permit holders (GOV.UK); public drinking can mean up to 6 months' prison or a QAR 3,000 fine. Note: alcohol is not on the customs.gov.qa tariff prohibited-goods list, and no Qatari-authority page stating the import ban was read; the verdict rests on three travellers' governments that agree.

limits.description: Narcotic and psychoactive medicines: up to 30 days' supply or the length of your stay, whichever is shorter. Psychotropic medicines: up to 2 months' supply. Needs a Ministry of Public Health permit, a prescription or medical report under 6 months old and a passport copy. Some substances are banned outright.

notes: Ministry of Public Health guideline (Pharmacy and Drug Control Department): drugs banned internationally and locally, and those in Sub-schedules A and B of Schedule 1 of Law No. 9 of 1987, may not be released. Prohibited items include cannabis, cannabis resin, heroin, LSD, psilocybin, cathinone, MDA and dronabinol. For patients arriving for personal use you need: a detailed approved medical report or prescription no more than six months old, showing patient details, diagnosis, treatment plan and duration, recommendations, scientific drug name, form, dose and quantity, stamped and on the health facility's letterhead; a signed undertaking that only you will use it; and a passport copy. 'An amount of narcotic and psychoactive substances sufficient for a maximum of thirty days or the duration of the patient's stay in the State of Qatar, whichever is shorter, is allowed' and 'An amount of psychotropic substances sufficient for a maximum of two months is allowed'. Any excess is destroyed by the department. The narcotic/psychoactive list includes amfetamine, dexamfetamine, codeine, dihydrocodeine, fentanyl, hydrocodone, hydromorphone, methadone, morphine, oxycodone and pethidine. The psychotropic list includes alprazolam, bromazepam, buprenorphine, clonazepam, diazepam, lorazepam, midazolam, temazepam, zolpidem, phentermine, phenobarbital, tramadol, pregabalin and gabapentin. The guide tells you to check INCB's Yellow and Green lists for updates. Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Concerta) and lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) are not named on the lists, so they are not included in names here. Permit: MOPH's Controlled Medicines System (https://fli.moph.gov.qa/traveller/home; user manual v1.0, 2025) takes applications from travellers carrying narcotic/psychotropic medicines for personal use. You upload passport, prescription, medical report and photos of the medicine; applications are 'reviewed within 24 hours'; an approved permit letter is 'valid for 90 days from date of approval' and 'must be printed and carried along with the original medical prescription and medical report during travel'. GOV.UK confirms the online permit system. The guideline PDF is dated Nov 2022; the controlling law is Law No. 9 of 1987.
